title: Flink & Stateful Stream Processing
interviewAnswer: Flink processes unbounded streams with state, event-time semantics, windows and checkpointing. It is designed for continuous computations where correctness across time and failures matters.
why: Flink questions test stateful stream processing, event-time reasoning and recovery beyond simply consuming Kafka messages.
intuition: Flink continuously processes events while maintaining state. Checkpoints make that state recoverable, and event-time/watermarks let windows reason about when events actually occurred.
deepDive: Operators transform streams; keyed streams partition state by key. Stateful operators snapshot state/checkpoint metadata to durable storage. Event time handles out-of-order events; watermarks estimate event-time progress; windows group events over time intervals. Exactly-once guarantees require source/state/sink coordination and depend on the full pipeline, not Flink alone.
workedExample: Radiation readings keyed by sensor can maintain rolling state and classify risk; a watermark allows late readings within a tolerated delay to update event-time windows.
commonMistakes: Confusing processing time with event time.
Claiming exactly-once without considering the sink.
Ignoring checkpoint size/recovery cost for large state.
followUps: How does Flink recover after failure?
production: Monitor checkpoint duration/failures, backpressure, watermark lag, state size and Kafka consumer lag; tune parallelism from bottlenecks.
